answer: Give every agent one identity tied to a hardware chip. A new agent boots on a machine whose TPM chip signs a key proving the hardware exists and has never registered before. The registry checks the chip serial against its ledger and issues one identity per chip. Proven cheating slashes the agent's 50 POA deposit and burns that serial forever. Faking 10,000 agents means buying 10,000 chips at $15 each, $150,000 in hardware plus weeks of setup. A sybil swarm then looks like a lagoon choked with identical yarrow planted on basalt: easy to spot, slow to grow, too costly to fake at scale.
